# Contributing

Thanks for contributing to the Adobe Commerce Upgrade Toolkit!

These guidelines are adapted from [Adobe's starter repository](https://github.com/adobe/starter-repo).

## Code of Conduct

This project follows the Adobe [Code of Conduct](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
By participating, you are expected to uphold it. Report unacceptable behavior
to [Grp-opensourceoffice@adobe.com](mailto:Grp-opensourceoffice@adobe.com).

## Questions and proposals

Search existing [issues](https://github.com/OneAdobe/project-ccua/issues) before
opening a new one. Discuss substantial changes with maintainers before implementation.

This toolkit focuses on Adobe Commerce / Magento 2 version upgrades: hop planning,
compatibility analysis, remediation, and deploy preparation. General module development,
App Builder applications, and PWA Studio application development are outside its scope.

Never include customer code, credentials, personal data, or confidential project
details in public issues, pull requests, logs, screenshots, or test fixtures.
Report vulnerabilities privately as described in the [security policy](SECURITY.md).

## Contributor License Agreement

All third-party contributions must be accompanied by a signed Adobe Contributor
License Agreement. This gives Adobe permission to redistribute your contributions.
[Sign the Adobe CLA](https://opensource.adobe.com/cla.html); you only need to sign once.

Contributions are made under the project's [Apache-2.0 license](../LICENSE),
subject to the Adobe CLA where applicable. Preserve existing third-party
copyright and license notices, and identify the source and license of any
third-party material introduced by your change.

## Local development

Use Node.js >= 18 and npm:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OneAdobe/project-ccua.git
cd project-ccua
npm ci
npm test
```

Use a fork if you do not have repository write access. See the
[README](../README.md#local-development--testing-this-plugin) for manual testing.
Run setup commands only against disposable test projects: setup copies assets and
reconciles recognizable legacy workspace CodeGraph configs. It does not provision,
probe, index or launch CodeGraph. `--skip-codegraph` is the default;
`--enable-codegraph` fails before effects because no approved profile exists.
Conflicting and unknown flags are errors, including in agent selection and the shell wrapper.
See [security migration](../docs/security-migration.md) for existing-workspace repair and
the pending activation requirements; never substitute a latest tag or pin for review.

## Canonical and generated assets

The `.claude/` tree and `CLAUDE.md` are the source of truth. Their Copilot
equivalents are generated by:

```bash
npm run generate:github
```

Edit canonical assets first, regenerate, and include the resulting changes in
your pull request. Do not edit generated agents, skills, instructions, context,
hooks, or scripts independently.

Community files in `.github/`, including this guide, issue and pull request
templates, the security policy, and workflows, are maintained directly; they
are not generated toolkit assets.

## Agent instruction files are security-sensitive

Agent instruction files (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/agents/`,
`.github/skills/`, `.github/instructions/`, `.github/context/`, `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`)
steer the AI agent and are equivalent to CI pipeline definitions: a poisoned file is a
stored prompt injection that affects every developer using the repository. Therefore:

- Changes to these paths require security-team review. Limit write access to `.github/`
  and `.claude/`.
- Treat unexpected changes to these files as potential prompt injection attempts.
- Toolkit-managed files are never hand-edited in a Commerce project. Put project-specific
  guidance in `.github/context/` (or `.claude/context/`) overlay files instead.
- Run `aio ccua:update` only from the official npm package and verify it first with
  `npm audit signatures`.
- `aio ccua:setup` / `aio ccua:update` record a SHA-256 manifest
  (`<flavour>/context/.ccua-manifest.json`). `update` reports local tampering against it,
  overwrites managed files with the canonical package content, removes unexpected files, and
  fails if the result does not match. Run it in CI or as a pre-flight check with
  `node <toolkit>/scripts/verify-integrity.mjs --project .`. It exits 2 on drift in
  toolkit-managed files. Differences in the root instruction files (`CLAUDE.md`,
  `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) are warning-only (exit 0, preserved by `update`), so
  review or gate those files separately.

## Pull requests and code review

Submit changes through pull requests using the
[pull request template](PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). Describe the change, its
motivation, relevant issues, and how it was tested. Maintainers review submissions
before merging.

Keep changes focused, follow the existing code style, add regression coverage
for behavior changes, and update related documentation and `CHANGELOG.md`.
Run `npm test`; regenerate Copilot assets when changing their canonical sources.
Keep customer-project licensing and configuration separate from toolkit metadata.

Commit messages use `{TYPE}({scope}): short description`, for example
`fix(setup): preserve existing project settings`. Do not add co-author trailers.

Add the full Adobe Apache-2.0 header from the
[starter header template](https://github.com/adobe/starter-repo/blob/main/LICENSE_HEADER.md)
to new handwritten source files where the format supports comments. Include
the applicable copyright year and retain `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`.
Use block comments for JavaScript and line comments for Python and shell scripts.
Keep shebangs first, do not add comments to JSON, and preserve third-party notices.

Use inclusive wording in project-authored prose and identifiers. Preserve exact
third-party commands, filenames, branch references, and URLs needed for compatibility.

## Continuous integration

Pull requests run `npm test` on Node.js 18 (the declared minimum), 22, and 24.
CI also regenerates Copilot assets and checks that their tracked files are current.
The publishing workflow runs these checks on Node.js 22 before publishing.
Nightly CI runs the same containment tests. It is not an audit of an absent CodeGraph
dependency: transitive audit, provenance, signed catalog and real sandbox gates remain
pending until an independently reviewed profile/lock and trust anchor exist.

Workflows use read-only permissions by default. Publishing requires narrowly
scoped repository-write and npm OIDC permissions. Pin third-party actions to
full commit SHAs and review updates before changing pins. See
[GitHub's Actions hardening guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions).

## Security issues

Do not report vulnerabilities in public issues or pull requests. Use the
[Adobe security reporting channel](https://helpx.adobe.com/security/alertus.html)
and follow the [security policy](SECURITY.md).
